title: NEB Class 11 Biology — Floral Diversity — 2024
subject: biology
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Classify the five kingdoms of living organisms. Give one characteristic feature of each.
questions.solution: **Monera** — prokaryotic, unicellular (bacteria). **Protista** — eukaryotic, mostly unicellular (algae, amoeba). **Fungi** — heterotrophic, chitin walls (mushrooms). **Plantae** — autotrophic, cellulose walls (mosses to angiosperms). **Animalia** — heterotrophic, no walls (sponges to mammals).

questions.question: Describe the general characteristics of the phylum Bryophyta. Give two economic importances.
questions.solution:
Small non-vascular plants; dominant gametophyte; need water for fertilisation; thalloid or leafy (Marchantia, Funaria).

**Importance:** Sphagnum peat (fuel, packing, seedbeds); ornamentals and traditional medicine.
questions.knowledgeNote: 'Amphibians of the plant kingdom' — tied to water for reproduction.

questions.question: Distinguish between gymnosperms and angiosperms with two examples of each.
questions.solution:
**Gymnosperms:** naked seeds on cones, no flowers/fruits — e.g. *Pinus*, *Cycas*. Mostly evergreen, wind-pollinated.

**Angiosperms:** seeds enclosed in fruits, true flowers — e.g. rice, mustard. Dominant, insect/wind pollinated, double fertilisation.
questions.knowledgeNote: Double fertilisation (embryo + triploid endosperm) is the angiosperm-exclusive signature.

questions.question: Write the general characteristics of Pteridophyta with two examples.
questions.solution: First true land plants with **vascular tissue** (xylem, phloem); dominant **sporophyte**; reproduce by spores (seedless vascular plants); need water for fertilisation. Examples: *Dryopteris* (fern), *Equisetum* (horsetail).
questions.knowledgeNote: 'Reptiles of the plant kingdom' — first vascular, still water-bound for sex.

questions.question: Classify algae into three major classes on the basis of pigments, with one example of each.
questions.solution:
**Chlorophyceae** (green — chlorophyll a/b): *Spirogyra*. **Phaeophyceae** (brown — fucoxanthin): *Sargassum*. **Rhodophyceae** (red — phycoerythrin): *Gracilaria*.

Pigment decides depth zones: red algae photosynthesise deepest.
questions.knowledgeNote: Agar (culture medium) and carrageenan (food gel) both come from red algae.

questions.question: Write the general characteristics of fungi. Give one beneficial and one harmful example.
questions.solution:
Eukaryotic heterotrophs with **chitin** walls; absorptive nutrition; reproduce by spores; body of hyphae (mycelium).

Beneficial: *Penicillium* (antibiotics). Harmful: *Puccinia* (wheat rust).
questions.knowledgeNote: Lichens (fungus + alga) are the symbiotic showcase — two kingdoms, one body.
